title: Tournament anti-Sidorenko orientations of trees with at most five branch vertices
affiliation: School of Mathematics, China University of Mining and Technology, Xuzhou, Jiangsu 221116, China
description: Editable English manuscript, necessary technical appendices, vector figures, rational certificate data, exact-arithmetic verifier and portable PDF build tools.
abstract: A finite tree with at most five vertices of degree at least three admits an orientation whose homomorphism density into any tournament is at most the random-tournament benchmark. Degrees, arm multiplicities and positive subdivision lengths are unrestricted, and a single orientation, chosen from the tree alone, satisfies the stronger kernel inequality for every finite probability space and every real skew kernel of absolute value at most one. For four branch vertices we convert terminal fourth moments into weighted second moments across a connector; for five we allocate reference arms in the star and fork skeletons and join the two halves of the path skeleton through compatible fractional moments. Separate arguments cover a central singleton arm and a unit outer connector. The kernel inequality also yields an entropy bound that holds for arbitrarily correlated vertex labels.
